levels.title: Artists with more than one hit (HAVING)
levels.task: The CEO wants to know how many artists have 2 or more songs on the top 50 list. Show the artist and the count of songs (song_count). Use HAVING to filter the aggregate functions after the GROUP BY.
levels.solution:
SELECT artist, COUNT(*) AS song_count
FROM top_songs
GROUP BY artist
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
levels.hintMessage: WHERE runs before GROUP BY. HAVING runs after the count—use it to drop small groups. Use HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 at the end of your query.
levels.successMessage: Great! HAVING keeps only artists with enough songs on the chart.

levels.title: Very new acts (MIN + HAVING)
levels.task: A&R at Stellar Sound wants artists whose first release date is after 2024-03-01. Show artist and the earliest release date (earliest_release). Use HAVING on that MIN date.
levels.solution:
SELECT artist, MIN(release_date) AS earliest_release
FROM top_songs
GROUP BY artist
HAVING MIN(release_date) > '2024-03-01'
levels.hintMessage: Use HAVING MIN(release_date) > '2024-03-01' at the end of your query.
levels.successMessage: Great! Every artist here is new on the chart after that date.

levels.title: CASE: viral or rising
levels.task: The social media team wants simple categories for songs released by Summit Records. Join top_songs to album_info on album_name. Show track_name, spotify_streams, and a new column called stream_status. Use CASE: if spotify_streams is 2000000000 or more, stream_status should be 'Viral'. Otherwise, stream_status should be 'Rising'. Only include songs where the label is 'Summit Records'.
levels.solution:
SELECT t.track_name,
  t.spotify_streams,
  CASE
    WHEN t.spotify_streams >= 2000000000 THEN 'Viral'
    ELSE 'Rising'
  END AS stream_status
FROM top_songs t
INNER JOIN album_info a ON t.album_name = a.album_name
WHERE a.label = 'Summit Records';
levels.hintMessage: CASE checks each row one at a time. Use WHEN spotify_streams >= 2000000000 THEN 'Viral'. Use ELSE 'Rising' for everything else.
levels.successMessage: Great work! You used a JOIN to filter by label and CASE to create readable stream categories.

levels.title: CASE: release quarter
levels.task: The analytics team wants to group 2024 songs by release quarter. Show track_name, release_date, and a new column called release_quarter. Use CASE to create these labels: dates from January through March = 'Quarter 1', April through June = 'Quarter 2', July through September = 'Quarter 3', and October through December = 'Quarter 4'. Only include songs released in 2024. ORDER BY release_date.
levels.solution:
SELECT track_name,
  release_date,
  CASE
    WHEN release_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-03-31' THEN 'Quarter 1'
    WHEN release_date BETWEEN '2024-04-01' AND '2024-06-30' THEN 'Quarter 2'
    WHEN release_date BETWEEN '2024-07-01' AND '2024-09-30' THEN 'Quarter 3'
    ELSE 'Quarter 4'
  END AS release_quarter
FROM top_songs
WHERE release_date LIKE '2024-%'
ORDER BY release_date;
levels.hintMessage: Start your CASE with: WHEN release_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-03-31' THEN 'Quarter 1'
levels.successMessage: Great work! CASE can turn raw dates into simple business categories like quarters.

levels.title: CASE and REPLACE with labels
levels.task: The playlist team is reviewing 2024 songs from Summit Records. Join top_songs to album_info on album_name. Show track_name, a cleaned-up artist name called artist_clean, and a new column called song_length. Use REPLACE to shorten every 'Kendrick Lamar' to 'K. Lamar'. Use CASE: if duration_ms is 200000 or more, song_length should be 'Long'. Otherwise, song_length should be 'Short'. Only include songs where the label is 'Summit Records'.
levels.solution:
SELECT t.track_name,
  REPLACE(t.artist, 'Kendrick Lamar', 'K. Lamar') AS artist_clean,
  CASE
    WHEN t.duration_ms >= 200000 THEN 'Long'
    ELSE 'Short'
  END AS song_length
FROM top_songs t
INNER JOIN album_info a ON t.album_name = a.album_name
WHERE a.label = 'Summit Records'
  AND t.release_date LIKE '2024-%';
levels.hintMessage: REPLACE changes the artist name text. CASE checks whether duration_ms is 200000 or more.
levels.successMessage: Awesome work! You combined a JOIN, REPLACE, and CASE in one query.
